assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth is the absolute densest planet in our entire Solar System
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about Earth's density. It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, name other major celestial objects, or address their main features or general composition. The fact is only tangentially related to the competency's broad topic.

copy.en: Earth is the absolute densest planet in our entire Solar System, packing a lot of mass!
copy.tl: Ang Earth ang pinakasiksik (densest) na planeta sa buong Solar System, puno ng mass!
copy.bis: Ang Earth mao ang pinakasiksik (densest) nga planeta sa tibuok Solar System, puno sa mass!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their density is less than the 1 g/cm3 density of water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and floating, which relates to matter, but it does not directly teach that matter has mass and takes up space. Density is a derived property, not the stated competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood and cork float because their density is less than the 1 g/cm3 density of water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about density and floating, with no mention of measuring distance or time, or using simple equipment for such measurements.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: density is less than the 1 g/cm3 density of water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions water (liquid) and air-filled spaces (gas) but does not identify or describe the three states of matter as solids, liquids, and gases. The focus is on density, not states of matter.

copy.en: Wood and cork float because their density is less than the 1 g/cm3 density of water! Wood has tiny air-filled spaces that lower its average density.
copy.tl: Lumulutang ang wood at cork dahil ang density nila ay mas mababa kaysa 1 g/cm3 density ng tubig! May maliliit na air-filled spaces ang wood.
copy.bis: Mulutang ang wood ug cork tungod kay ang density nila ubos sa 1 g/cm3 density sa tubig! Ang wood adunay gagmayng air-filled spaces.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: volume by water displacement
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use measuring cylinders or beakers to measure volume using units, such as milliliters (mL), and liters (L)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions measuring volume by water displacement but does not mention measuring cylinders or beakers, nor the units mL or L, which are the specific tools and units required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Measure its mass with a scale
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions measuring mass with a scale and uses g/cm3, but does not identify or appropriately use the specific units (mg, g, kg, °C) required by the competency. The density unit g/cm3 is not among the listed units.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Measure its mass with a scale
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card involves measuring, but it does not describe science process skills such as observing, predicting, and measuring using millimeter, centimeter, or meter units. The measurement here is of mass and volume, not length in the specified units.

copy.en: Wood has a density below 1 g/cm3, so it floats in water! Measure its mass with a scale and volume by water displacement, then divide mass by volume.
copy.tl: Ang kahoy ay may density na below 1 g/cm3, kaya lumulutang ito sa tubig! Sukatin ang mass gamit ang scale at volume gamit ang water displacement, tapos hatiin.
copy.bis: Ang kahoy adunay density nga below 1 g/cm3, busa mulutaw kini sa tubig! Sukta ang mass gamit ang scale ug volume gamit ang water displacement, unya bahina.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whether something floats depends not just on its weight, but on its density compared to the liquid!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and buoyancy, not the definition of matter as having mass and taking up space. It shares the broad topic of matter but does not directly support describing matter's mass/volume properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whether something floats depends not just on its weight, but on its density compared to the liquid!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe shape or volume properties of solids, liquids, or gases. It focuses on density and floating, which is not the competency's content.

copy.en: Whether something floats depends not just on its weight, but on its density compared to the liquid!
copy.tl: Ang paglutaw ng bagay ay hindi lang nakadepende sa bigat, kundi sa density nito kumpara sa likido!
copy.bis: Ang paglutaw sa butang dili lang nagsalig sa gibug-aton, kondili sa density niini itandi sa likido!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An object floats if its density is lower than water's, and sinks if its density is higher!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains floating/sinking in terms of density, but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. Density is related to matter but the competency's core definition is not taught.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An object floats if its density is lower than water's, and sinks if its density is higher!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density and buoyancy, not the physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. It shares the matter domain but does not directly support this competency.

copy.en:
Why do some things float while others sink?

An object floats if its density is lower than water's, and sinks if its density is higher!
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang iba habang ang iba ay lumulubog?

Lumulutang ang isang bagay kung mas mababa ang density nito kaysa sa tubig, at lumulubog kung mas mataas!
copy.bis:
Nganong ang uban molutaw samtang ang uban molunod?

Molutaw ang usa ka butang kon mas ubos ang density niini kaysa tubig, ug molunod kon mas taas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deposition is when a gas changes directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The competency lists melting, evaporation, freezing, and condensation as the changes of state to describe. Deposition (gas to solid) is not among these processes, so the card does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deposition is when a gas changes directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The competency focuses on temperature causing changes such as solid to liquid to gas. Deposition is a change of state but is not the solid→liquid→gas sequence described, and the card does not address temperature as the cause.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Deposition is when a gas changes directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires explaining changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes for solid→liquid→vapor and vapor→liquid→solid. Deposition (gas→solid) is not one of the listed transitions, and the card gives no particle or energy explanation.

copy.en: Deposition is when a gas changes directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first! It’s like water vapor turning into frost on cold grass. It is the reverse of sublimation.
copy.tl: Ang deposition ay pagbabago ng gas direkta sa solid nang hindi nagiging likido! Gaya ng singaw ng tubig na nagiging escarcha (frost) sa malamig na damo. Ito ang kabaligtaran ng sublimation.
copy.bis: Ang deposition mao ang pagbalhin sa gas direkta sa solid nga dili una mahimong likido! Sama sa alisngaw sa tubig nga mahimong escarcha (frost) sa bugnaw nga sagbot. Kabaliktaran kini sa sublimation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They break grease and oil into tiny droplets that water carries away
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how detergent/soap emulsify grease into droplets, which is about cleaning action and emulsions, not about describing uniform vs non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. It does not teach the classification or examples required by the competency.

copy.en: Detergent and soap work the same way! They break grease and oil into tiny droplets that water carries away, washing off stains from clothes and dishes.
copy.tl: Gumagana sa parehong paraan ang detergent at sabon! Hinahati nila ang langis at grasa sa maliliit na patak na tinatangay ng tubig, kaya nahuhugasan ang mantsa sa damit at plato.
copy.bis: Parehas og pamaagi ang detergent ug sabon! Bahinon nila ang lana ug grasa ngadto sa gagmay nga tinulo nga madala sa tubig, busa mahugasan ang mansa sa sinina ug plato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: kills worms living in the gut
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the gut but does not identify or describe the parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) or how they work. It only refers to worms in the gut, which is tangentially related to the digestive system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: kills worms living in the gut
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe how any human body system works, including the digestive system. It only mentions a medicine that kills worms in the gut, which is not direct instruction on the digestive system's function.

copy.en: There's a medicine called deworming that kills worms living in the gut, and schools often give it to kids.
copy.tl: May gamot na tinatawag na purga o deworming na pumapatay sa bulate sa bituka, at madalas itong ibinibigay sa mga bata sa paaralan.
copy.bis: Adunay tambal nga gitawag deworming nga mopatay sa bulate sa tinai, ug kasagaran ihatag kini sa mga bata sa eskwelahan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cells use sugar as fuel to make energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions glucose indirectly as 'sugar' and energy production, but does not describe homeostasis, its indicators (body temperature, glucose level, blood pressure), or the balance among body systems. It only touches on glucose as fuel, which is a peripheral concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cells use sugar as fuel to make energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that cells use sugar as fuel to make energy, which is a basic idea underlying respiration, but it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products. It provides background knowledge but does not directly teach the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: your body can move, think, and grow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions body functions (move, think, grow) but does not describe any of the listed human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) or how they work. The connection is too vague to support the competency.

copy.en:
Why do cells need the sugar insulin lets in?

Cells use sugar as fuel to make energy — so when insulin helps sugar get inside, your body can move, think, and grow!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng cell ang asukal na pinapasok ng insulin?

Ginagamit ng cell ang asukal bilang gatong para sa enerhiya — kaya kapag tinulungan ng insulin na makapasok ang asukal, nakakagalaw, nakakaisip, at nakakalaki ang katawan!
copy.bis:
Ngano gikinahanglan sa cell ang asukal nga gipasulod sa insulin?

Gigamit sa cell ang asukal isip gatong para sa enerhiya — mao nga kung tabangan sa insulin nga makasulod ang asukal, makalihok, makahunahuna, ug makatubo ang lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: cells stop responding to it well, so sugar builds up in the blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific disease (type 2 diabetes) involving high blood sugar due to insulin resistance. It does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it explain the concept of glucose level as a homeostatic indicator. It only provides an example of a disruption, which is related background but not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: In type 2 diabetes, insulin is still there, but cells stop responding to it well, so sugar builds up in the blood — it's the most common type, often linked to lifestyle.
copy.tl: Sa type 2 diabetes, may insulin pa rin, pero hindi na ito masyadong pinapansin ng mga cell, kaya naiipon ang asukal sa dugo — ito ang pinakakaraniwang uri, kadalasang nauugnay sa pamumuhay.
copy.bis: Sa type 2 diabetes, naa gihapon ang insulin, apan dili na maayo motagad ang mga cell niini, mao nga matigom ang asukal sa dugo — mao kini ang pinakakomon nga matang, sagad nalambigit sa estilo sa pagpuyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pancreas makes almost no insulin, so a person with Type 1 diabetes needs regular insulin injections instead.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a disease condition (Type 1 diabetes) and insulin treatment, but does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems, nor does it mention indicators such as glucose level, body temperature, or blood pressure. It only tangentially relates to glucose regulation, which is an indicator of homeostasis, but the card itself does not teach the concept of homeostasis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pancreas makes almost no insulin, so a person with Type 1 diabetes needs regular insulin injections instead.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how homeostasis is maintained through various feedback mechanisms, both positive and negative
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not explain how homeostasis is maintained through feedback mechanisms, positive or negative. It states a fact about insulin deficiency and replacement therapy, but does not discuss feedback loops, regulation, or maintenance of balance. It is only related to the broader topic of glucose regulation.

copy.en:
What happens in Type 1 diabetes?

The pancreas makes almost no insulin, so a person with Type 1 diabetes needs regular insulin injections instead.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa Type 1 diabetes?

Halos hindi na gumagawa ng insulin ang pancreas, kaya kailangan ng taong may Type 1 diabetes ng iniksyon ng insulin.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa Type 1 diabetes?

Halos wala nay insulin nga mahimo sa pancreas, mao nga kinahanglan og iniksyon sa insulin ang tawo nga adunay Type 1 diabetes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diamonds form deep inside the Earth, where the heat and pressure are extremely high!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a rock/mineral (diamond) but does not involve exploring school grounds, collecting rocks, or describing texture, color, or grain crystal size. It only states where diamonds form, which is not the skill of observing/collecting rocks.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diamonds form deep inside the Earth, where the heat and pressure are extremely high!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to name and describe the upper crustal layers of the solid earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the deep Earth but does not name or describe the upper crustal layers of the solid earth. It does not support the competency's focus on crustal layers; it only gives a general fact about diamond formation.

copy.en: Diamonds form deep inside the Earth, where the heat and pressure are extremely high!
copy.tl: Ang diamante ay nabubuo sa napakalalim na bahagi ng Lupa, kung saan napakataas ng init at presyon!
copy.bis: Ang diyamante mabuhat sa lalom kaayo nga bahin sa Yuta, diin grabe ka taas ang init ug presyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A child should keep eating during diarrhea to have the strength needed to recover.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives health advice about continuing to eat during diarrhea, mentioning food as a source of strength. It does not teach students to identify the basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) as a general concept. The connection to food as a basic need is incidental and not the instructional focus.

copy.en:
Should you stop eating during diarrhea?

No! A child should keep eating during diarrhea to have the strength needed to recover.
copy.tl:
Dapat bang huminto sa pagkain kapag may pagtatae?

Hindi! Dapat patuloy pa ring kumain ang bata habang may pagtatae para magkaroon ng lakas na kailangan para gumaling.
copy.bis:
Kinahanglan ba mohunong pagkaon kung nagkalibang?

Dili! Ang bata kinahanglan padayon sa pagkaon samtang nagkalibang aron adunay kusog nga kinahanglan aron mauli-an.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: two atoms of the same element are covalently bonded together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of covalent bonds using a molecule of water and a molecule of carbon dioxide
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions covalent bonding but does not explain the formation of covalent bonds using water and carbon dioxide as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some elements like oxygen exist as diatomic molecules (O₂)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical name of some common covalent compounds, including water (H2O), carbon dioxide (CO2), and ammonia (NH3)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives O₂ as an example of a covalent compound but does not address writing chemical formulas and names of the required common covalent compounds such as water, carbon dioxide, and ammonia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some elements like oxygen exist as diatomic molecules (O₂)!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card touches on elements and compounds but does not describe fixed chemical composition or the unique number of protons for atoms of an element as required by the competency.

copy.en: Some elements like oxygen exist as diatomic molecules (O₂)! This means two atoms of the same element are covalently bonded together.
copy.tl: Ang ilang elemento gaya ng oxygen ay umiiral bilang diatomic molecule (O₂)! Ibig sabihin, dalawang atomo ng parehong elemento ang covalent na nagbi-bond.
copy.bis: Ang ubang elemento sama sa oxygen naglungtad isip diatomic molecule (O₂)! Pasabot niini, duha ka atomo sa samang elemento ang covalent nga nagbugkos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it is used as a solvent and aerosol spray propellant
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some useful things that people have made from non-living materials and describe what natural materials have been used to make the items
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a useful product (solvent/propellant) but does not describe what natural materials were used to make it, so it does not directly support identifying useful things made from non-living materials and their source materials.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diethyl ether is an ether with an oxygen atom between two ethyl groups
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the chemical structure and uses of diethyl ether, not physical properties of solid materials such as hard, shiny, or stretchable. Diethyl ether is a liquid, and no solid-material physical properties are addressed.

copy.en: Diethyl ether is an ether with an oxygen atom between two ethyl groups, and it is used as a solvent and aerosol spray propellant.
copy.tl: Ang diethyl ether ay isang ether na may oxygen atom sa pagitan ng dalawang ethyl groups, at ginagamit ito bilang solvent at aerosol spray propellant.
copy.bis: Ang diethyl ether usa ka ether nga adunay oxygen atom tali sa duha ka ethyl groups, ug gigamit kini isip solvent ug aerosol spray propellant.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The scent molecules spread from the kitchen through the whole house by diffusion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a diffusion example but does not describe the particle model properties (constant motion, spaces, attraction, or temperature dependence) that the competency requires. It only mentions molecules spreading, which is a phenomenon explained by particle motion, not a direct teaching of the competency's content.

copy.en:
Why can you smell yummy adobo from another room?

The scent molecules spread from the kitchen through the whole house by diffusion, bringing that delicious smell right to your nose!
copy.tl:
Bakit maaamoy mo ang masarap na adobo mula sa kabilang kwarto?

Kumakalat ang mga molekula ng amoy mula sa kusina patungo sa buong bahay sa pamamagitan ng diffusion, kaya naaamoy mo siya!
copy.bis:
Nganong masimhutan nimo ang lami nga adobo gikan sa pikas kwarto?

Mikatag ang mga molekula sa humot gikan sa kusina ngadto sa tibuok balay pinaagi sa diffusion, mao nga masimhutan nimo kini!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: stirring the water mixes the dye much faster than diffusion by itself!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mixing dye in water and the effect of stirring, but does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. It does not directly support the competency's focus on classifying everyday mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diffusion alone is slow, so stirring the water mixes the dye much faster than diffusion by itself!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions diffusion and mixing, which relate to particle motion, but it does not describe particles being constantly in motion, having spaces, attracting each other, or moving faster with temperature increase. It does not directly teach the particle model concepts in the competency.

copy.en:
Why do we stir water when mixing dye?

Diffusion alone is slow, so stirring the water mixes the dye much faster than diffusion by itself!
copy.tl:
Bakit natin hinalo ang tubig kapag naglalagay ng tina?

Ang diffusion lamang ay mabagal, kaya kapag hinalo natin ang tubig, mas mabilis kumalat ang tina kaysa diffusion lang!
copy.bis:
Nganong nato kutawon ang tubig kon magbutang og tina?

Ang diffusion lang hinay, mao nga kon kutawon nato ang tubig, mas paspas mosagol ang tina kaysa diffusion lamang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sharp teeth mean it ate meat, while flat teeth mean it ground up plants.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how tooth shape indicates meat-eating vs plant-eating, which touches on carnivore/herbivore concepts, but it does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources to classify animals. It is a specific paleontological inference about dinosaurs, not direct instruction for the competency's grouping task.

copy.en:
How do scientists know what dinosaurs ate?

By studying their teeth! Sharp teeth mean it ate meat, while flat teeth mean it ground up plants.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng mga siyentista ang kinain ng dinosaur?

Sa pamamagitan ng pag-aaral ng mga ngipin nito! Ang matatalas na ngipin ay para sa karne, habang ang patag na ngipin ay para sa paggiling ng halaman.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nahibaloi sa mga siyentista ang gikaon sa dinosaur?

Pinaagi sa pagtuon sa iyang ngipon! Ang hait nga ngipon alang sa unod, samtang ang patag nga ngipon alang sa paggaling og tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds are living descendants of dinosaurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that birds are descendants of dinosaurs, which touches on common ancestry, but it does not explain or use lines of evidence such as fossils, biogeography, or comparative morphology to support evolution. It does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds are living descendants of dinosaurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses dinosaur extinction and bird ancestry but does not describe natural selection as the primary mechanism driving evolutionary change. No selection, adaptation, or mechanism is addressed.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds are living descendants of dinosaurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not discuss concepts such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, or adaptation in the context of evolutionary theory. It only states a fact about bird ancestry, which is related to evolution but not to the specific concepts listed.

copy.en:
Are all dinosaurs really extinct?

Not quite! All non-avian dinosaurs died out millions of years ago, but birds are living descendants of dinosaurs — so birds count as dinosaurs too!
copy.tl:
Talaga bang lahat ng dinosaur ay wala na?

Hindi lahat! Namatay na ang mga non-avian na dinosaur milyong taon na ang nakalipas, pero ang mga ibon ay buhay na inapo ng dinosaur — kaya sila ay dinosaur din!
copy.bis:
Tinuod ba nga nawala na ang tanang dinosaur?

Dili tanan! Namatay na ang mga non-avian nga dinosaur milyong tuig na ang milabay, pero ang mga langgam buhi nga kaliwat sa dinosaur — mao nga sila dinosaur usab!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dinosaurs roamed the Earth for over 150 million years, with the last ones dying out about 66 million years ago.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a specific fact about dinosaur duration and extinction, but does not explain how the geologic time scale helps recount Earth's history. It lacks any mention of the time scale, its divisions, or how it is used to organize Earth's history. The fact could be used as an example within such an explanation, but the card itself does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dinosaurs roamed the Earth for over 150 million years, with the last ones dying out about 66 million years ago.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss as a class how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions extinction of dinosaurs, but the competency is about discussing how threats to biodiversity can lead to species extinction. The card does not discuss threats, biodiversity, or the process of extinction; it only states a historical fact. It does not support a class discussion on biodiversity threats.

copy.en: Dinosaurs roamed the Earth for over 150 million years, with the last ones dying out about 66 million years ago.
copy.tl: Nabuhay ang mga dinosaur nang mahigit 150 milyong taon, at namatay ang huli sa kanila mga 66 milyong taon na ang nakalipas.
copy.bis: Nabuhi ang mga dinosaur sulod sa kapin 150 ka milyon ka tuig, ug namatay ang kataposan nila mga 66 ka milyon ka tuig na ang milabay.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all animals died out with the dinosaurs—birds, crocodiles, and other small animals survived
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to explain how lines of evidence, such as fossils, biogeography, and comparative morphology, support the occurrence of evolution
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about survival after dinosaur extinction but provides no lines of evidence (fossils, biogeography, comparative morphology) and does not explain evolution. It shares the broad topic of living things but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: birds, crocodiles, and other small animals survived
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions birds and crocodiles but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, etc.). It does not teach classification by similar characteristics, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Not all animals died out with the dinosaurs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the geologic time scale helps to recount the history of the Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card references a past extinction event but does not explain the geologic time scale or how it recounts Earth's history. It is only tangentially related to geologic time.

copy.en: Not all animals died out with the dinosaurs—birds, crocodiles, and other small animals survived, and their relatives are still around today.
copy.tl: Hindi lahat ng hayop ay namatay kasabay ng mga dinosaur—nakaligtas ang mga ibon, buwaya, at iba pang maliliit na hayop, at may mga kaliwat pa rin sila ngayon.
copy.bis: Dili tanang hayop nangamatay uban sa mga dinosaur—nabuhi ang mga langgam, buaya, ug uban pang gagmay nga hayop, ug aduna pay mga kaliwat karon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A dinosaur's teeth reveal its diet: sharp teeth mean it ate meat, flat teeth mean it ground up plants.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how teeth indicate diet (meat vs. plants) but does not group animals into herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores, nor does it use secondary sources as required by the competency. It provides background knowledge about diet inference but does not directly support the grouping skill.

copy.en:
How can we tell what a dinosaur ate?

A dinosaur's teeth reveal its diet: sharp teeth mean it ate meat, flat teeth mean it ground up plants.
copy.tl:
Paano malalaman kung ano ang kinakain ng dinosaur?

Sinasabi ng hugis ng ngipin kung ano ang kinakain ng dinosaur: matalim na ngipin para sa karne, at malapad para sa pagdurog ng halaman.
copy.bis:
Unsaon nato masayran kung unsa ang gikaon sa dinosaur?

Ang porma sa ngipon sa dinosaur nagpakita kon unsa ang gikaon niini: hait nga ngipon para sa karne, ug patag para sa pagdugmok og tanom.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A vaccine trains your body to recognize and fight a germ
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the body fighting a germ but does not describe any of the specified systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory). It is about immune response and disease spread, not the listed body systems.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When many people get vaccinated, a disease has a harder time spreading!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how vaccination reduces disease spread, which is an interaction between living things (people and germs) that brings good. However, it does not explain the interaction itself or the good/harm mechanism; it only states a public-health outcome. It does not directly teach the competency's concept of interactions bringing good or harm.

copy.en:
Why do vaccines matter?

A vaccine trains your body to recognize and fight a germ without getting seriously sick first. When many people get vaccinated, a disease has a harder time spreading!
copy.tl:
Bakit mahalaga ang bakuna?

Sinasanay ng bakuna ang katawan na kilalanin at labanan ang germ nang hindi muna nagkakasakit nang malubha. Kapag marami ang nabakunahan, mahirap nang kumalat ang sakit!
copy.bis:
Nganong hinungdanon ang bakuna?

Ang bakuna nagbansay sa lawas nga mailhan ug masukol ang germ nga dili una grabe magmasakiton. Kon daghan ang nabakunahan, lisod na mokaylap ang sakit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's called dispersion! That's when white light splits into all its different colors.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines dispersion (splitting of white light into colors), which is a phenomenon related to refraction through prisms, but the competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection and refraction using mirrors, blocks, lenses, and prisms with everyday examples. The card does not teach reflection, refraction, or any investigation/illustration, so it only shares the broad topic of light behavior.

copy.en:
What do we call it when white light splits into different colors?

It's called dispersion! That's when white light splits into all its different colors.
copy.tl:
Ano ang tawag kapag nahahati ang puting liwanag sa iba't ibang kulay?

Dispersion ang tawag dito! Ito yung paghahati ng puting liwanag sa magkakaibang kulay.
copy.bis:
Unsay tawag kung ang puti nga kahayag mabahin ngadto sa lahi-laing kolor?

Dispersion ang tawag ani! Mao ni ang pagbahin sa puti nga kahayag ngadto sa lahi-laing kolor.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Fine salt (like table salt) dissolves faster than big chunks! Tiny grains have more surface touching the water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses how particle size (surface area) affects the rate of dissolving, not the solubility (maximum amount of solute that can dissolve in a solvent at equilibrium). The competency G7-M-10 focuses on factors affecting solubility, with heat as the example. Surface area is a kinetic factor affecting dissolution speed, not solubility, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

copy.en: Fine salt (like table salt) dissolves faster than big chunks! Tiny grains have more surface touching the water.
copy.tl: Mas mabilis matunaw ang pinong asin (parang table salt) kaysa malalaking buo-buo! Mas maraming bahagi ng maliliit na butil ang nadidikit sa tubig.
copy.bis: Mas paspas matunaw ang pino nga asin (sama sa table salt) kaysa dagkong tipik! Mas daghan ang bahin sa gagmayng lugas nga modikit sa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a physical change! It's still sugar, and the water still tastes sweet.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies dissolving sugar as a physical change and gives a reason (still sugar, sweet taste), but it does not explain why physical changes are reversible and chemical changes are irreversible. The competency requires an explanation of reversibility/irreversibility, which the card does not address.

copy.en:
Is dissolving sugar in water a physical or chemical change?

It's a physical change! It's still sugar, and the water still tastes sweet.
copy.tl:
Pisikal ba o kemikal ang pagkatunaw ng asukal sa tubig?

Pisikal na pagbabago! Asukal pa rin ito, at matamis pa rin ang tubig.
copy.bis:
Pisikal ba o kemikal ang pagkatunaw sa asukal sa tubig?

Pisikal nga kabag-ohan! Asukal man gihapon kini, ug matam-is gihapon ang tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: each oil part boils at a different temperature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions boiling and vaporization but does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state generally (solid to liquid to gas). It focuses on fractional distillation of oil fractions, not the state-change concept itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Separation works because each oil part boils at a different temperature
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why separation works by different boiling points, but it does not demonstrate any of the listed separation techniques (decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, using magnets). Distillation is not among the techniques in this competency.

copy.en: Separation works because each oil part boils at a different temperature! The ones that turn to vapor easily rise up, while the harder-to-boil parts stay near the bottom.
copy.tl: Gumagana ang paghihiwalay dahil ang bawat bahagi ay kumukulo sa magkaibang temperatura! Ang madaling sumingaw ay umaakyat, habang ang mahirap sumingaw ay nananatili sa ilalim.
copy.bis: Molihok ang pagbulag tungod kay ang matag bahin mobukal sa lahi nga temperatura! Ang sayon mosingaw mosaka, samtang ang lisod mobukal magpabilin sa ubos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: minerals in hard water get in the way and stop bubbles from forming easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses why soap lathers better in distilled water than hard water, but it does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. The mention of minerals in water is only tangentially related to mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: minerals in hard water get in the way and stop bubbles from forming easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions minerals in water, which could imply dissolved substances, but it does not identify the role of solute and solvent in a solution. It does not teach which component is the solute or solvent or explain their roles.

copy.en: Soap makes bigger, better bubbles in distilled water! That's because minerals in hard water get in the way and stop bubbles from forming easily.
copy.tl: Mas malaki at mas maganda ang bula ng sabon sa distiladong tubig! Kasi ang mga mineral sa matigas na tubig ay nakakasagabal sa pagbuo ng bula.
copy.bis: Mas dako ug mas nindot ang bula sa sabon sa distiladong tubig! Kay ang mga mineral sa gahi nga tubig makababag sa paghimo og bula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diwata-1 was the very first Philippine microsatellite! It was designed and built by Filipinos and sent into space in 2016.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a Filipino invention (a microsatellite) but does not identify any specific scientist or their invention, which is the core action of G4-M-1. It only mentions that Filipinos designed and built it, so it is related to science inventions but does not directly support identifying a scientist.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Diwata-1 was the very first Philippine microsatellite! It was designed and built by Filipinos and sent into space in 2016.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies including telescopes and space probes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a space technology (microsatellite) and its launch, but does not explain how modern research about celestial objects uses new space technologies such as telescopes and space probes. It does not discuss research methods or celestial objects, so it only shares vocabulary about space technology without directly supporting the competency.

copy.en: Diwata-1 was the very first Philippine microsatellite! It was designed and built by Filipinos and sent into space in 2016.
copy.tl: Ang Diwata-1 ang pinaka-unang microsatellite ng Pilipinas! Dinisenyo at ginawa ito ng mga Pilipino at inilunsad sa kalawakan noong 2016.
copy.bis: Ang Diwata-1 mao ang pinaka-unang microsatellite sa Pilipinas! Gidisenyo ug gibuhat kini sa mga Pilipino ug gipadala sa kawanangan niadtong 2016.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: DNA has a double-helix shape
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models and labeled diagrams to represent the double helix structure of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that DNA has a double-helix shape with an analogy. The competency requires using models and labeled diagrams to represent the double helix structure. The card provides no model, diagram, or representation activity, so it does not directly support the competency's action.

copy.en:
What shape is DNA?

DNA has a double-helix shape — like a ladder that's been twisted round and round!
copy.tl:
Ano ang hugis ng DNA?

Ang DNA ay may hugis na double helix — parang hagdan na pinilipit paikot!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang porma sa DNA?

Ang DNA adunay porma nga double helix — sama sa hagdan nga gilikoliko!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Just four "letters" called bases — A, T, C, and G
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models and labeled diagrams to represent the double helix structure of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the four nucleotide bases and their order, but does not address the double helix structure of DNA, nor does it use models or labeled diagrams as required by the competency.

copy.en:
What spells out the DNA code?

Just four "letters" called bases — A, T, C, and G — and the order they're arranged in spells out all the instructions.
copy.tl:
Ano ang bumubuo sa code ng DNA?

Apat lang na 'letra' na tinatawag na bases — A, T, C, at G — at ang pagkakasunod-sunod nila ang bumubuo ng mga tagubilin.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang naghimo sa code sa DNA?

Upat lang ka 'letra' nga gitawag og bases — A, T, C, ug G — ug ang ilang pagkasunod-sunod mao ang naghimo sa mga panudlo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The double-helix structure of DNA was discovered in 1953.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models and labeled diagrams to represent the double helix structure of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the year the DNA double helix was discovered. It does not use models or labeled diagrams, nor does it describe the structure itself, so it does not directly support the competency of representing the double helix structure.

copy.en:
When was DNA's shape discovered?

The double-helix structure of DNA was discovered in 1953.
copy.tl:
Kailan natuklasan ang hugis ng DNA?

Natuklasan ang double-helix na hugis ng DNA noong 1953.
copy.bis:
Kanus-a nadiskobrehan ang porma sa DNA?

Ang double-helix nga porma sa DNA nadiskobrehan niadtong 1953.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Don't stop a test early just because you like the result! That makes it unfair.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize the features of a fair test and that scientific investigations also involve doing at least three trials, or use replication, and observing, measuring, and recording accurately
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses fairness in a test by advising not to stop early, but it does not teach the specific features listed in the competency: at least three trials, replication, or observing, measuring, and recording accurately. It is only tangentially related to the fair-test concept.

copy.en: Don't stop a test early just because you like the result! That makes it unfair. Always finish the planned time for every single run.
copy.tl: Huwag tigilan ang test nang maaga kung gusto mo na ang resulta! Hindi iyon fair. Palaging tapusin ang nakatakdang oras para sa bawat takbo.
copy.bis: Ayaw hunonga ang test kay ganahan na ka sa resulta! Dili na fair. Kanunay human-a ang nakatakda nga oras para sa matag dagan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Never drop animals or people to test falling!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: predict and explain whether heavier objects will fall faster than lighter objects due to the force of gravity
assignedReviews.reason: The card is a safety warning about not dropping living things during falling-object tests. It does not teach prediction or explanation of whether heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects due to gravity, nor does it provide any content about gravity or falling patterns. It only touches the same general topic of falling objects.

copy.en: Never drop animals or people to test falling! We only test objects, and a safe classroom drop is enough to see the pattern!
copy.tl: Huwag magbuhos ng hayop o tao para subukan ang paghulog! Mga bagay lang ang sinusubukan, at sapat na ang ligtas na classroom drop para makita ang pattern!
copy.bis: Ayaw paghulog og hayop o tawo aron sulayan ang paghulog! Mga butang ra ang atong sulayan, ug igo na ang luwas nga classroom drop aron makita ang pattern!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Different dog breeds can have totally different fur, ear shapes, and body sizes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes variation among dog breeds, not classification of living things into named groups (mammals, reptiles, etc.) using a table. It does not support the classification skill or the required table format.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Different dog breeds can have totally different fur, ear shapes, and body sizes!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions variation in traits, which is a concept in evolution, but it does not discuss heredity, isolation, selection, adaptation, or any other key evolutionary concept, nor does it support a small-group discussion of these theories.

copy.en: Different dog breeds can have totally different fur, ear shapes, and body sizes!
copy.tl: Magkaiba ang balahibo, hugis ng tainga, at sukat ng katawan ng iba't ibang lahi ng aso!
copy.bis: Lahi-lahi ang balhibo, porma sa dalunggan, ug gidak-on sa lawas sa nagkalainlaing kaliwat sa iro!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A dog has many tiny muscles around each ear, letting it lift, lower, and turn its ears
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses ear muscles enabling ear movement, but G3-L-4 focuses on observing and describing outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in moving and gathering food. Ears are not presented as outer body parts used for locomotion or food gathering; the card is about muscle anatomy, not the outer part's role.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A dog has many tiny muscles around each ear, letting it lift, lower, and turn its ears
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: G4-L-1 requires describing how human body systems (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) work. The card is about dog ear muscles, not human body systems, and does not explain how the muscular system works in general. It only mentions that many muscles allow ear movement, which is not direct support for describing the human muscular system.

copy.en:
Why can dogs move their ears so easily?

A dog has many tiny muscles around each ear, letting it lift, lower, and turn its ears — dogs have far more ear muscles than people, which is why we can barely wiggle ours!
copy.tl:
Bakit kaya ng aso na malayang igalaw ang tainga?

May maraming maliliit na kalamnan sa paligid ng bawat tainga ng aso, kaya kaya nitong iangat, ibaba, at ikilos ang tainga — mas marami silang kalamnan sa tainga kaysa sa tao, kaya halos hindi natin maigalaw ang atin!
copy.bis:
Nganong sayon ra sa iro nga ilihok ang dalunggan?

Aduna silay daghang gagmay nga kaunoran libot sa dalunggan para pag-isa, pagpaubos, ug pagliko. Mas daghan silag kaunoran kaysa tawo, mao nga lisod tang molihok sa atong dalunggan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dogs have sharp hearing and can hear high sounds that people cannot hear at all.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a dog's hearing ability, but does not describe outer body parts (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement and food gathering. Hearing is not an outer body part used for movement or food gathering.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dogs have sharp hearing and can hear high sounds that people cannot hear at all.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about hearing high sounds, which relates to sound perception, but it does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred. It only states a comparative hearing ability, not the mechanism of sound production or transfer.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dogs have sharp hearing and can hear high sounds that people cannot hear at all.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sensory ability of dogs, but does not address the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). Hearing is not one of the listed characteristics, and the card does not support teaching these characteristics.

copy.en: Dogs have sharp hearing and can hear high sounds that people cannot hear at all.
copy.tl: Ang aso ay may matalas na pandinig at nakaririnig ng mga matataas na tunog na hindi naririnig ng tao.
copy.bis: Ang iro adunay talas nga pagdungog ug makadungog sa hataas nga mga tingog nga dili madunggan sa tawo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Dogs are clever! With good training, they can learn all kinds of commands and cool tricks.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about dogs learning tricks and commands, which is a specific behavior, not about the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It does not directly support describing these characteristics.

copy.en: Dogs are clever! With good training, they can learn all kinds of commands and cool tricks.
copy.tl: Matalino ang mga aso! Kapag sinanay nang mabuti, natututo silang gumawa ng iba't ibang utos at trick.
copy.bis: Maalamon ang mga iro! Kung maayo silang bansayon, makakat-on sila og lain-laing mando ug trick.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: About 9 weeks — around 63 days!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the duration of a dog's pregnancy. It does not compare life-cycle stages from birth to adulthood, nor does it address birds or plants, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How long are dogs pregnant?

About 9 weeks — around 63 days!
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal magbuntis ang aso?

Mga 9 na linggo — humigit-kumulang 63 araw!
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay magmabdos ang iro?

Mga 9 ka semana — mga 63 ka adlaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A dog's sense of smell is incredibly strong
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a dog's sense of smell, which is not an outer body part and does not describe the role of any outer body part in movement or gathering food. It shares the broad topic of animals but provides no direct instructional support for observing or describing outer body parts or their functions.

copy.en: A dog's sense of smell is incredibly strong — it can sniff out things that people simply cannot smell at all.
copy.tl: Napakatalas ng pang-amoy ng aso — nakakaamoy ito ng mga bagay na hindi kayang maamoy ng tao.
copy.bis: Hilabihan ka talas ang panimaho sa iro — nakasimhot kini sa mga butang nga dili masimhutan sa tawo.
